checks.result: valid under the stated finite-dimensional hypotheses
checks.details: For overlapping supports, a partial vacuum bra annihilates every vector in the tensor excitation subspace, including entangled vectors. Thus elementary creations commute and overlapping products vanish. Commuting adjoint maps move a support disjoint from p to the innermost commutator. In each surviving expanded word, created sites outside p remain excited and supports on either side of V_p are disjoint. At most |p| creations fit on each side, giving depth 2s and the exact output-sector form.

checks.result: valid; constants independent of sector dimension
checks.details: Apply the triangle inequality only across input tuples, and Cauchy--Schwarz over mutually orthogonal output sectors within each tuple. If u lies in p, n>=0 and |p|<=s yield gamma0. If u lies outside p but in M_j, n>=1 and |M_j|<=n+s imply |M_j|/(n+t)<=(s+1)/(t+1). Summing the D|M_j| possible interactions cancels the inverse |M_j| factor. Each remaining support costs s times its per-site norm; summing the k choices of j yields beta_k=2^k(gamma0*s^k+k*gamma1*s^(k-1)). k=0 uses only the first case.

The BCH expansion is a finite exact polynomial. Since [C,H0]Omega has sector -H0^M c_M, the displayed KT equation has the correct sign. The multilinear estimate gives both the self-map bound and Lipschitz constant lambda*q_s prime(r)<1/2. The finite family of coefficient spaces is complete; e^(-C)Omega has vacuum coefficient one.

Write e^C phi=(B+b0)Omega. Subtracting the ground equation produces [H0,B]Omega-epsilon[B,W(C)]Omega=delta B Omega after nonvacuum projection. The term [C,H0] commutes with B. For |delta|<Delta/2, the inverse is bounded by 2/(Delta|M|), so the sector estimate yields ||B||_1<=2 lambda q_s prime(r)||B||_1<||B||_1. This excludes delta=0 multiplicity and every eigenvalue within Delta/2. The uniform contraction on the real segment gives a continuous simple branch from the unperturbed ground eigenvalue; finite-dimensional eigenvalue continuity excludes a ground-state crossing.

Finite tensor products of nonnegative compact-resolvent operators have a product eigenbasis and compact resolvent. Spectral cutoff tensor spaces preserve interaction support and do not increase interaction norms. Their nested union is an operator and form core because the perturbation is bounded. For sufficiently large cutoff the first two Ritz values exist when the full dimension is at least two, and each converges by min--max. Their positive uniform difference passes to the limit and forces simplicity. The manuscript separately treats a one-dimensional full space. No uniform control of the cutoff-dependent creation operators is required.

checks.details: Dominant highest weights have a nonzero fundamental-weight coefficient; subtracting that fundamental weight leaves a dominant weight. Positivity of the A_(N-1) fundamental-weight Gram matrix proves C2(Lambda)>=C2(omega_i)>=C_F, including N=2. The uniform coefficient is 2b_N/C_F<=8N^2/(N^2-1)<=32/3. Four link factors per plaquette and two incident plaquettes per coordinate plane give s=4,D=2(d-1); side lengths >=2 and distinguished positive-direction link factors exclude small-torus identifications. The scale factor x C_F/2 converts the normalized gap 1/2 into x C_F/4. The unique ground line carries a continuous character of a product of SU(N) groups, which is trivial. Restricting the excitation inequality to the physical subspace therefore preserves the gap. Vertex grouping has three distinct sites and D=3 binomial(d,2).

The result is a finite-volume spectral inequality with constants independent of dimensions/volume; it does not claim convergence of infinite-volume ground states, a GNS Hamiltonian at the explicit threshold, a continuum limit, or uniformity at fixed Nx.
